title: IDF Chief Visits Gaza-Border Surveillance Soldiers, Cites Duty to 'Listen Carefully' as Oct. 7 Lesson
detail: IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited female surveillance soldiers of the 414th Combat Intelligence Collection Unit at Re'im Base on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, telling them 'you are our eyes on the front, the first to identify infiltration threats and activate forces' and that 'one of the lessons of October 7 is that we must listen carefully to every female and male soldier as part of assessments and the decision-making process.' The visit followed renewed complaints from surveillance soldiers — some of whom attribute the dismissal to sexism — that warnings they raised about current Gaza-border threats are again being brushed aside, echoing accounts that spotters' alerts about Hamas's October 7 attack preparations went unheeded before the assault.

title: Netanyahu Orders UNRWA Jerusalem Training Center Dismantled, Citing Oct. 7 Involvement
detail: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 that he had ordered the dismantlement of a UNRWA vocational training center in the Kafr Aqab area of East Jerusalem, following National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir's earlier announcement of the move. Netanyahu said Israel 'will not allow an organization whose employees were involved in terrorism and in the October 7 massacre to operate on its territory, and will take action against it using every means at its disposal,' invoking the 2024 Israeli law banning UNRWA from operating on Israeli territory. Israeli officials have repeatedly accused a portion of UNRWA staff of participating in the October 7 attack; a UN internal investigation previously found 9 of 19 investigated employees may have been involved and terminated them, while a separate review found insufficient evidence for Israel's broader claims about the agency's workforce. UNRWA denies the accusations. Ben Gvir said police were working to clear the 82-dunam site, which the Jerusalem municipality has approved for a road and 'educational complex'; UNRWA says Jordan granted it the land in 1952 and warned the takeover would violate UN facilities' legal protections.

media.caption: Israeli forces move to take over the UNRWA vocational training center in Kafr Aqab, East Jerusalem, August 25, 2026
